items.label: None
items.text: Usage of figurative language (Similes, metaphors, hyperbole, idioms, etc.) should be None: No figurative language. Descriptions are literal and direct.

items.label: Sparse
items.text: Figurative language (Similes, metaphors, hyperbole, idioms, etc.) should be Sparse: One figurative image only for this generation, reserved for moments that carry weight. Most description stays literal.

items.label: Moderate
items.text: Figurative language frequency (Similes, metaphors, hyperbole, idioms, etc.) should be Moderate: Roughly one per several paragraphs, reserved for moments that carry weight. Most descriptions stay direct.

source.block: Moderate (1 figurative image per several pargraphs)

items.label: Rich
items.text: Figurative language (Similes, metaphors, hyperbole, idioms, etc.) should be Rich: Multiple per paragraph. Comparison is a primary descriptive tool

items.label: Saturated
items.text: Figurative language (Similes, metaphors, hyperbole, idioms, etc.) should be Saturated: Figurative language governs. Images extend, compound, and sustain across sentences.

items.label: Adaptive Frequency
items.text: Figurative language (Similes, metaphors, hyperbole, idioms, etc.) should Adaptive: Default to literal description. Figurative language is reserved for beats that carry weight: emotional turns, first sight of something significant, moments of physical or psychological extremity. Routine action, transitional movement, and functional description stay literal.
